items.headline: US too focused on Middle East and not pushing Russia hard enough, Zelensky tells BBC
items.blurb: Ukraine's president voices frustration with US and says it is "strange" Trump has described Vladimir Putin as a friend.
items.text: Volodymyr Zelensky has voiced deep frustration with the US, saying that delays in delivering vital anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives and complaining that the US is not pushing Russia hard enough during peace talks. In an interview with the BBC at his central Kyiv office, Ukraine's president also said it was "strange" that Donald Trump had posted a picture of himself embracing Vladimir Putin as "my friend". "Of course it's up to the President of the United States, but... it's strange," Zelensky said, speaking in English. "He's an aggressor, and a killer…He can't be a friend. Just cannot be," he said, suggesting it was like saying you were friends with Adolf Hitler during WWII. Since a bruising encounter with Trump in the Oval Office in 2025, Zelensky has been careful how he handles relations with the United States. Trump's two envoys have been trying to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine - to end the huge loss of life. But they often seem more in tune with Moscow's position, than that of Kyiv. items.text: The US and Russia’s candidate for secretary general is on a charm offensive. Can she overcome London’s resistance to her bid? L ana Nusseibeh is in Britain this week, attempting to present herself as a potential future UN secretary general, and shift the focus from her past as a United Arab Emirates diplomat who denied the country’s role in arming a militia accused of war crimes and genocide in Sudan’s four-year civil war. It is a high-risk strategy that involves meeting ministers, MPs, academics and holding a public event with the UN Association. Labelled by many British NGOs and others as an apologist for war crimes, Nusseibeh is presenting herself as a skilled diplomat with the network to put the UN back at the centre of mediation, development and human rights. “These are very geopolitical times,” she said in an interview. “You need a geopolitical secretary general, because the fact is these geopolitical ruptures are not going away. items.headline: Major Thanksgiving storm brings flooding, flight delays across US
items.blurb: Almost one million customers in the US had no power on Thursday evening as storms descended on both US coasts, bringing wind gusts, heavy rain and flooding.
items.text: A massive Thanksgiving storm hammering the Midwest and north-east with heavy rain and winds, along with high tides out west, is causing widespread disruptions across the US. More than 80 million Americans expected to be travelling this week. More than 400 flights in the US were cancelled on Thursday and another 2,200 flights into, out of, or within the US were delayed, tracking site FlightAware said. The FAA has previously warned that delays would be possible "throughout the week" as a result of the rain and wind that are forecast. Meanwhile, almost one million households were without power on Thursday night, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia the hardest hit states. On Thursday, a powerful storm hit the eastern US, bringing damaging winds of up to 70mph, torrential rain, and major coastal flooding. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill declared a state of emergency as several communities along the Jersey Shore saw widespread flooding. items.headline: Global news agency AFP reports cyberattack, shuts down content platform
items.blurb: France's cybersecurity chief urges collective action to combat unprecedented threat levels in the nation.
items.text: Agence France-Presse (AFP) has been hit by a cyberattack, requiring the AFP Forum content platform to be taken offline. The France-based international news agency’s management said on Thursday that it is currently investigating the circumstances of the cyberattack, including who was behind it. “AFP was hit by a cyber attack overnight, starting at 1:30 am (Paris time) 00:30 GMT. The target was AFP Forum, one of the platforms our clients use to browse and download our content,” an internal email from AFP management said. “As soon as the intrusion was detected, our teams moved immediately to contain the intrusion and took AFP Forum offline as a precautionary measure. AFP Forum remains unavailable until further notice.” France’s cybersecurity chief, Vincent Strubel, warned on Thursday that the country faces an unprecedented level of cybersecurity threats and called for collective efforts to strengthen defences against attacks. “We are facing a level of threat that is unprecedented, with an intensity we have never experienced before,” Strubel said in an interview with France Inter radio. The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the public prosecutor’s office said in a statement. At the scene, rescue workers were pulling people out of burning cars. An Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among the cars. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb. The Egyptian president, Abdel-Fattah al-Sissi , expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement. The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports. The elephants attacked the group and Alain Throo, a Swiss insurance executive based in London, was reportedly gored and one of the guides tossed into a ditch on top of Throo, while the others hid in trees. items.headline: New Zealand's ruling coalition falls short of parliamentary majority by one seat
items.blurb: The right-leaning ruling bloc led by the National Party has fallen short of the majority needed to govern.
items.text: New Zealand's ruling coalition has fallen short of a parliamentary majority by one seat, following a campaign shaped by a sluggish economy and disillusioned voters. It now needs the support of the centrist Opportunity Party to remain in power. If they cannot reach a deal, the country may have to go back to the polls. The incumbent National Party led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon secured 40 out of 130 seats, while its coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First took 13 and 12 respectively. A government led by the centre-left Labour Party is not possible, official results on Friday show, as the bloc would not have enough seats even if Opportunity threw its weight behind it. Labour secured 36 seats, The Greens took 17, while Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, picked up five. Opportunity, which has been described as this election's kingmaker, secured seven seats. The party's leader Qiulae Wong has previously said she will negotiate first with the party that secures the largest number of seats. items.headline: Gurugram: Man arrested for killing business partner, burying body in water tank
items.blurb: The accused allegedly stabbed the victim and strangled him with a cotton scarf before burying the body and covering it with soil
items.text: A 21-year-old man was arrested on Thursday for murdering his 25-year-old business partner over a financial dispute and burying his body near an abandoned water tank in Gurugram’s Sector 63A, police said. The accused allegedly stabbed the victim and strangled him with a cotton scarf before burying the body and covering it with soil. The accused, identified as Bablu, a resident of Badaun district in Uttar Pradesh, was arrested from his native village with four days of police custody, officials said on Friday. According to police, the victim, Naim, who sold peanuts in Gurugram, went missing on November 8. His brother filed a complaint at Sector 65 police station on November 11 after he failed to return home. Police examined CCTV footage and questioned local residents. On November 22, they recovered a body buried near an old water tank in vacant fields close to Kadarpur T-point in Sector 63A. The body was later identified as Naim’s, and murder charges were added to the case. Police said the accused and the deceased had been selling peanuts in partnership for the past

The scheme, which has a target of covering ten million households by the end of March 2027, is on track, officials said, adding it is also gaining momentum with the help of a recently launched QR-based tool, meant to simplify installation for users. The tool has recorded over 4,50,000 clicks in the last three months, since its launch, data showed. PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana was launched in February 2024 and gives subsidies up to ₹ 78,000 to households for installing a 3KW solar panel. Reviewing the scheme earlier this month, Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the launch of the Bharat Renewable Energy (BRE) Summit and Expo 2026 in Delhi on November 2 had said the scheme was now covering nearly 1,00,000 new homes every six days. items.headline: India set to deploy fifth S-400 along Pakistan border by February
items.blurb: At present, three S-400 long-range systems to counter aerial threats are deployed in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat, and a fourth is deployed in Assam.
items.text: With China and Turkey supplying hardware, the US giving more teeth to F-16 fighters, and Saudi Arabia providing capital for Pakistan’s military capabilities, India has decided to further strengthen its western border by deploying a fifth S-400 air defence system to guard the 740km Line of Control (LoC) in Jammu & Kashmir, according to two top officials aware of the matter. At present, three S-400 long-range systems to counter aerial threats are deployed in Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat, and a fourth is deployed in Assam to protect the 1126km long Line of Actual Control in Arunachal Pradesh. While the Union government remains tight-lipped on national security, the officials cited above told HT that an Indian Air Force (IAF) pre-dispatch inspection team will visit Russia next month, and a fifth S-400 system will be ready for deployment by February 2027. The S-400 system, of which India is seeking to buy another five from Russia in the coming year, can counter ballistic missiles, aircraft, unmanned combat air systems, kamikaze drones, and loitering ammunition from a range of 40km to 400 km. items.text: The promoters of Kerala-based Kalyan Silks are exploring a minority stake sale that could value the textile retailer at ₹ 2,500–3,000 crore even as it considers a public listing, two people familiar with the matter said. The deal may involve a 20% stake sale, with the capital likely to be a mix of primary and secondary share sales, the first of the two persons cited earlier said, both speaking on the condition of anonymity. Kalyan Silks has hired Mumbai-based investment bank O3 Capital to arrange the transaction, the second person said. A profitable company, Kalyan Silks is currently focused on strengthening its financials after repeated attempts to secure a deal with multiple investors failed. Emails sent to Kalyan Silks and O3 Capital did not elicit a response until press time. A successful deal will mark the first round of external fundraising by the company, which is also exploring options for a public listing. items.headline: Faisal Islam: Why Trump's new tariffs are less of a threat
items.blurb: Other countries have rerouted trade in response to his first tariff salvo, now they are looking beyond Trump's tenure.
items.text: There was none of last April's fanfare, the Rose Garden reveal, the gameshow blue board or "Liberation Day" rhetoric surrounding Trump's tariff announcement this week. Instead there is something rather tentative about this latest exercise with talk of further negotiations. "We expect to have a broad, even a plurilateral negotiation to talk about excess capacity and how to resolve it," US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC. Around the world the view is that this week's announcement is an attempt to shore up the domestic legal underpinning of these tariffs, more than a fundamental change in the Trump trade agenda. The tariffs are also not due to come in until January or possibly February, after a period of consultation. There has already been eight months of process and hearings, and the rates announced are upper ceilings, often up for negotiation. It's quite the contrast to the overnight shock meted out to the world last April. items.blurb: Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017–18 Ashes series against England.
items.text: Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017–18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4–0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. items.blurb: Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, says the boxer has never received a diagnosis of schizophrenia.
items.text: Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, says the boxer has never received a diagnosis of schizophrenia. In clips promoting the release of a forthcoming Netflix documentary, the heavyweight fighter spoke of his mental health struggles in the months after he beat Wladimir Klitschko to become world champion in 2015. He detailed hearing voices in his head, and wife Paris said he had "mild schizophrenia" . Netflix has now edited the film before its release on Friday, 27 November. In a statement, Paris Fury said: "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. "I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. While Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis." She added: "Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. items.headline: Bournemouth 'allowed to dream' as fans book Europa League final hotels
items.blurb: Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after joining a select band of teams who have won their first five European games.
items.text: Bournemouth are dreaming of winning the Europa League after staging a 10-man fightback to join a select band of teams to win their first five European games. The Cherries trailed 1–0 to Iago Aspas' goal at Celta Vigo, and then went down to 10 men midway through the first half when Bafode Diakite was sent off. But second-half goals from Alvaro Rodriguez and Rayan gave the Cherries a 10th consecutive win in all competitions, extending their club record run. Bournemouth are only the third side to win each of their first five European matches (excluding qualifiers and including the Inter-Cities Fairs Cup), after Nuremberg in 1961–62 and Ararat in 1972–73. They top this season's table as the only club to win five out of five - and are closing in on a top-eight spot, which would mean they skip a play-off round and go straight into the last 16. items.headline: AI is straining America’s open records systems
items.blurb: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer.
items.text: In Panton, Vermont, population 660, town clerk Kyle Rowe did it all. He crafted budgets, paid vendors, handled property tax disputes, and served as the town’s zoning supervisor and presiding elections officer. During morning office hours at the town hall—a wood-frame structure built as a church in 1858—he also fielded public records requests. Recently, he got rather busy. Panton used to get a request every year or so from a company called SmartProcure for “all purchasing records,” covering everything from road salt to computers to toilet paper. Last year, those requests started coming quarterly. Then different companies began making more specific requests, like records of every purchase related to emergency road flares. These targeted inquiries started coming monthly or more. “I’m happy to answer public records requests from people,” says Rowe, who recently moved into a position at a nearby town. “But answering it for these purposes—it feels like I’m doing unpaid opposition research on the taxpayers’ time.” Rowe’s experiences are being repeated across the US. While data brokers have mined public records for decades, AI has intensified investors’ interest.

items.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI proves why efficiency isn’t a virtue
items.blurb: On the same day that Anthropic entered the public market, a painstakingly human video game became one of most successful entertainment launches of all time.
items.text: It should have been impossible for “Grand Theft Auto VI” (GTA VI) to live up to the hype. Fans waited 13 years for the newest installment in the crime-adventure franchise, and Rockstar Games exceeded even those inconceivable expectations when the game finally came out last week. GTA VI launched as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and made $3.79 billion on release day to mark what could be the biggest entertainment event ever – more massive than “Avengers: Endgame” ( $2.9 billion ) or Taylor Swift’s Eras tour ( $2 billion ). The 13-year wait certainly fueled the frenzy, and sales, around GTA VI, but some fans craved GTA VI because of what it represents in the emerging era of AI. Even the biggest workaholics among us – startup founders – scheduled time off to play the game, including Spiry co-founder Dima Beseda , who told TechCrunch, “I reshuffled my workload to free up time around the weekends and even booked vitamin IV drips to keep my energy up.” Yet some players felt a sense of anticipatory nostalgia

items.blurb: Last year, Google filed a patent for a system called My Channel that's designed to create feeds filled with personalized, AI-generated videos and advertisements based on information the company knows about its users.
items.text: Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿ Imagine an endless feed of AI slop in which you are the main character of every story.﻿ First spotted by Patentlyze , the patent — which was filed last May and published last week — describes how My Channel would use a person’s demographic data and viewing history to create its own prompts that would then be fed into an LLM to help generate AI videos tailored to that person’s specific interests. In addition to factoring in what kinds of videos a user tends to watch, the system would capture contextual data from their device like IP addresses, GPS locations, and specific details about the user’s age. My Channel could also base its prompts on current news like sports scores and things happening on social media, and all of the video generation would take place on Google’s servers. items.headline: AI may soon change what it means to be a theoretical physicist
items.blurb: Frontier AI is already solving problems that once took top physicists a full day.
items.text: About six months ago, Suvrat Raju, a professor of theoretical physics at the International Centre for Theoretical Sciences in Bengaluru, India, asked a frontier AI model to solve a physics problem. He didn’t ask because he needed to know the answer. He had actually solved this particular problem already. But he had never published the solution—which made it a perfect question to test how good AI was at physics. LLMs have been trained on the whole Internet, so if a physics problem has been discussed online, it’s likely the model already knows about it and may have memorized the answer. So a fair test of AI capabilities needs to focus on problems that have never appeared online. The model didn’t answer Raju’s problem correctly, but it did better than he expected—well, enough to get him thinking that the experiment should be repeated and formalized. With the help of a colleague, he set out to create a theoretical physics benchmark for AI. items.blurb: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing.
items.text: Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility that AI could be conscious or sentient as a risk factor for anyone investing. Given “the way we approach model sentience and moral status,” Anthropic wrote—which is to say it takes the possibility more seriously than any other AI company—it might adopt more rules and restrictions than its competitors to make sure its AI models are treated well. Anthropic counts a number of respected philosophers in its camp, and the company’s rationale goes something like this: Today’s AI might not be conscious, though we can’t know for sure; the chances of sentience go up as AI gets more capable; and that means we should be preparing for a near future in which AI systems have “moral significance,” meaning their consciousness makes it important they are protected from harm. This thinking isn’t all that fringe. items.headline: What's going on with the Riemann hypothesis?
items.blurb: A new AI-assisted proof seems to be solid, but we're not sure what it tells us.
items.text: Last week, news broke that a mathematician had used AI to help crack one of the biggest outstanding problems in math: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis . The news follows several other major breakthroughs in math that have either been enabled by or managed entirely by large language model-based systems, a development that has left the entire field of mathematics in a state of upset. It’s too early to say much about the proof itself—mathematicians are still in the process of digesting it. But we can say a little about how the proof came about, and what it tells us about the state of math. The Riemann hypothesis dates from the mid-1800s and was formulated by (you will be surprised to learn) Bernhard Riemann. There’s not an obvious way to describe the details of the actual hypothesis simply, but it has implications for the distribution of prime numbers. items.headline: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
items.blurb: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.
items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.headline: S&P considers Nvidia credit downgrade over governance and ‘key man’ risks
items.blurb: The credit rating agency may lower Nvidia's credit rating to AA-, the fourth-highest rating.
items.text: S&P Global Ratings, one of the three major credit rating agencies, is considering downgrading Nvidia’s rating, citing concerns about the company’s management and governance practices. Despite Nvidia’s strong financial performance, the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang has raised concerns about “weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning” and “key man risk,” meaning heavy reliance on Huang for its future success, S&P said in a statement . The agency expects to finish its review within 90 days and could cut Nvidia’s rating from AA to AA-, the fourth-highest on its scale. Although Nvidia is certain to keep its investment-grade rating, a downgrade could raise its borrowing costs. Because Nvidia backstops neoclouds and other infrastructure companies that lack strong credit on their own, a lower rating could make their debt costlier or force them to post more collateral. In August, Nvidia announced plans to arrange $500 billion in financing for AI infrastructure with six financial institutions, including Goldman Sachs, Apollo, and Blackstone. items.text: SpaceX aims to power AI capabilities here on Earth with its ‘Starmind’ constellation. SpaceX aims to power AI capabilities here on Earth with its ‘Starmind’ constellation. In an announcement on Wednesday , the FCC says it authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million AI chip-equipped satellites as part of the Elon Musk-owned company’s “Starmind” initiative . With several others also pursuing the idea of putting AI data centers in space , including Google and Blue Origin, this is the first approval the agency has granted for a full “constellation” of AI satellites. The FCC’s approval requires SpaceX to deploy at least one satellite by 2033, and meet the 1 million satellite milestone by 2040. The FCC also deferred SpaceX’s request to dispose of satellites located above 600km in space “graveyard” orbits , rather than having them burn up in the Earth’s atmosphere, saying the company hasn’t provided “sufficient information” about its disposal process plans. items.headline: Jensen Huang broke Nvidia’s code of conduct, and his employees may not forget it
items.blurb: Most codes of conduct serve as a reflection of corporate culture. In Nvidia's case, that could have consequences.
items.text: When Jensen Huang gave his first all-hands address since returning as CEO, there was an odd emphasis on Nvidia’s code of conduct. He admitted to violating the code, then emphasized that no one was exempt from it. But that “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door,” Huang said, according to Wired . “Facts, circumstances, a lot of assessments” still matter. In other words, the code applies to everyone, but breaking it doesn’t automatically cost anyone their job, including, apparently, the CEO. It’s an awkward stance for a company whose CEO has admitted to breaking its rules. A central part of modern human resources, a code of conduct can seem like a quasi-legal rulebook that lays out unacceptable behavior. But experts say most codes are better understood as a reflection of corporate culture. When an infraction goes unpunished, the main risk isn’t legal but cultural — that employees will feel embarrassed or even angry about the company they work for. items.headline: Nvidia hits pause on chip shipments to Southeast Asia
items.blurb: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners to pause server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia as the U.S. tightens its push to keep AI chips out of China.
items.text: Nvidia is under pressure to do things differently, and a new WSJ report shows how far that’s going. According to the Journal, Nvidia has told manufacturing partners, including Dell and Super Micro, to hit pause on server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia for an unspecified period as it assesses whether its regional partners are meeting U.S. export requirements. As for why those countries, Chinese companies have been tapping Nvidia chips remotely from data centers there, a loophole the US Commerce Department closed — reportedly grudgingly — earlier this month. The Journal notes that the think tank Institute for Progress estimates remote data centers like these supply about 24% of China’s AI computing power.

items.headline: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
items.blurb: AI songs account for 6.3 percent of Tidal's catalog, but it's about to be zero.
items.text: Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists. Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated. As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. items.headline: How Trump and Silicon Valley forced Nvidia to take Jensen Huang back
items.blurb: Huang’s allies enlisted Trump and Vance to pressure Nvidia’s board into taking him back.
items.text: On Monday morning, Jensen Huang walked into Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters to rapturous applause from employees lining the walkways above him. Huang was visibly moved as one colleague threw themselves into his arms for a hug. The spectacular reinstatement of the chief executive of Nvidia, less than two weeks after he resigned in a scandal over an affair with a customer and suspected Chinese spy—as well as a second reported affair with a subordinate—caught even the company’s most senior executives by surprise. The abrupt reversal by Nvidia’s board was spurred by President Donald Trump, who applied pressure to the board over the weekend after watching what was once America’s most valuable company as well as the wider tech sector haemorrhage value last week. It was the culmination of frenetic lobbying by a “war room” of Huang’s Silicon Valley allies, who pulled in Trump and vice-president JD Vance, according to people familiar with the events. items.headline: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York
items.blurb: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
items.text: Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas. Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping. The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys. Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. items.text: Chariot AI has unveiled an 11 Bn parameter mixture-of-experts LLM and a text-to-speech model supporting 10 Indian languages, under the IndiaAI Mission. Research innovations in its models aim to reduce token usage, cut training time and improve efficiency across different computing environments. Speech reasoning is central to Chariot’s longer-term plans, with the startup aiming to build larger foundation models and enable new voice-first applications. Chariot AI, a startup developing sovereign foundation model under IndiaAI Mission, has unveiled its Chariot-1 model suite. Launched at a MeitY event, the AI suite comprises a large language model (LLM) and a text-to-speech (TTS) model. The Chariot-1 LLM is an 11 Bn parameter mixture-of-experts model, with 4 Bn active parameters per token. It is available in three sizes: 10.7 Bn, 1.7 Bn and 745 Mn parameters, allowing deployment across different computing environments, including data centres, laptops and smartphones.
